item.title: 21 Years Later, Anime’s Forgotten 50-Episode Vampire Masterpiece Deserves a Second Look
item.description: Vampires are among horror's most enduring monsters, yet in anime, they remain surprisingly underrepresented. That's not to say there aren't excellent examples, of course. Vampire Hunter D: Bloodlust is one of the most gorgeous early-2000s anime films ever made, while the original 1985 Vampire Hunter D also remains an all-timer. Later series like Shiki and Kizumonogatari similarly dove into the bloodthirsty realm of vampires in their own fascinating ways, while the more recent Castlevania brought one of the most infamous video game vampires to animation.

item.title: 007 First Light's Brilliant Tutorial Is a Game Direction Miracle
item.description: The 007 First Light tutorial is the platonic ideal of a perfect video game tutorial. IO Interactive reveals how it came together.

item.title: Stephen King's Near-Perfect 2-Part Thriller Is Officially Being Removed From Netflix
item.description: Widow’s Bay was one of the most discussed shows of the year. Set on a small island, the series is a mix of seemingly opposing genres, following Mayor Tom Loftis (Matthew Rhys) as he tries to reshape the cursed town of Widow’s Bay into a worthwhile vacation spot. Throughout its episodes, the series straddles the line between comedy and horror, pairing hilarious workplace banter with a horrifying cursed party. It’s a show that owes equally to Parks and Rec and the mythos of Stephen King .

item.title: 12 Years Later, Hbo's Near-Perfect Vampire Series Still Has an Unwatchable Ending
item.description: My passion for HBO’s True Blood eventually led me to visit an alleged vampire’s grave in real life. I started watching the summer before my senior year of college in 2010, and by the time I visited Mercy Brown’s grave in Exeter, Rhode Island, I was into vampires enough to get college credit for it.

item.title: Alan Ritchson's Reacher Officially Hits Major Milestone Ahead of Season 5
item.description: Alan Ritchson has had a busy year. Between seasons of Prime Video's Reacher , he's taken starring roles in numerous film and TV projects , including Netflix's sci-fi thriller War Machine and the action comedy Runner. But of course, his best-known role is the wandering renegade Jack Reacher, and the role has earned him praise from Amazon and MGM Studios' top executives . In a 2024 interview, Jennifer Salke, head of Amazon and MGM Studios, told The Hollywood Reporter , “ We’ll have Alan as long as he will play Jack Reacher. No end in sight for that, hopefully that’s for a very, very, very long time.”

item.title: 30 Years Later, Star Trek's Greatest 'Next Generation' Movie Is Officially Free to Stream
item.description: Turning a successful television series into a movie isn't as easy as just giving the cast a bigger budget and adding in more explosions. What works on the small screen doesn't always translate to theaters, especially when filmmakers lose sight of what made audiences fall in love with the characters in the first place. Fortunately, Star Trek : First Contact understood that bigger could be better, provided the spectacle didn't come at the expense of the characters.

item.title: 8 Sci-Fi Books That Get Even Better the Second Time You Read Them
item.description: Science fiction is a genre built on far-out ideas, strange new worlds, and scientific possibilities that can fundamentally change how we understand our own. Some of the most unforgettable sci-fi novels offer just as much intrigue on a second reading as they do on the first. Whether it's a carefully constructed mystery, an intricate timeline, or a seemingly insignificant detail that takes on entirely new meaning once you know the ending, such books reward readers willing to go back for another speculative look.

item.title: 7 Funniest 'Far Side' Comics About Food
item.description: Anything can be the star of a Far Side comic . While most of them featured stupid humans or talking animals as their main characters, the surrealist streak in cartoonist Gary Larson sometimes gave life to inanimate objects as well. For example, there’s a strip where a jogger tells a living pair of scissors that they can no longer run together. And if scissors can be alive in The Far Side comics, just about anything can, including food.

item.title: 8 Classic PlayStation Games That Are Barely Playable Today
item.description: If you’ve ever watched someone play an old PlayStation game and wondered why their character keeps spinning around in circles, congratulations, you’ve already met tank controls. If you’re unfamiliar, here’s your quick introduction: With tank controls, pressing up moves your character forward in whatever direction they’re facing, and pressing left or right only rotates them, so with the stick alone, you can’t sidestep or turn on a dime. That’s manageable in a hallway. It’s much less so when you’re sneaking past a guard, lining up a shot, or timing a leap across a pit, which is why the same scheme caused trouble in just about every genre during the PS1 era. These eight classic games are the hardest to go back to, whether the culprit is tank controls or something else entirely.
